endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Establish a freshness and update cadence — clinical guidelines, formularies, and protocols change, and stale retrieval corpora produce outdated outputs.

endorsements.title: AI agents in clinical practice: an evidence map
endorsements.quote: Concrete steps include integration into medical education curricula, standardized agent disclosures prior to institutional procurement, post-deployment benchmarking, and behavioral audit trails for drift detection.

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement from the ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR & RSNA
endorsements.quote: Autonomous AI should be designed to initiate actions that are transparent, identifiable, and discoverable.

endorsements.title: Medical AI Agents for Clinical Decision Support: Viewpoint Using the Planning, Action, Reflection, and Memory (PARM) Analytical Lens
endorsements.quote: Complete auditability requires recording not only agent outputs but also the reasoning processes, data sources, and intermediate steps that led to those outputs [ 30 ].

evidence.title: Performance, Failures, and Oversight of a Large Language Model Agent for Clinical Data Analysis: Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Undisclosed agent actions such as postcrash rerun, detectable only via execution logs
evidence.effect: Result text accurately reflected execution logs in nearly all runs, though unit propagation and an undisclosed postcrash rerun were identified.
evidence.quote: Result text accurately reflected execution logs in nearly all runs, though unit propagation and an undisclosed postcrash rerun were identified.

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether keeping and reviewing per-action run traces and replay logs detects or reconstructs erroneous agent actions. One simulated study of 27 agent runs found an undisclosed postcrash rerun that was visible only in execution logs, which suggests the hazard exists but does not show that log review prevents harm.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice. The single related study is a level 4, offline or simulated analysis of 27 agent runs in the United Kingdom. It documents the hazard and does not compare organizations that review logs with those that do not. Certainty about the practice's benefit cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

In the simulated runs, result text matched execution logs in nearly all cases, yet reviewers found unit propagation and an undisclosed postcrash rerun only in the logs. This suggests that agent summaries may omit actions that matter. Whether routine log review would catch such errors before they reach patients has not been measured.

The hazard study relied on execution logs to find undisclosed actions, which indicates that such logs can be informative when someone reads them. No study reports how much reviewer time trace review takes, what fraction of traces get reviewed in practice, or how often reviewers correctly reconstruct an error in a live clinical workflow.

Two commentaries endorse the practice. The radiology multi-society statement asks that autonomous AI actions be transparent, identifiable, and discoverable, and the PARM viewpoint asks that reasoning, data sources, and intermediate steps be recorded. The cited CHAI playbook language addresses retrieval corpus update cadence and does not speak directly to run traces. None of these sources report outcome data.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare trace retention with structured review against usual practice in deployed clinical agents, and that report the rate of erroneous actions detected, time to reconstruction, reviewer burden, storage cost, and downstream patient harm.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. The one hazard study listed older adults and used simulated runs, so it offers no information on whether trace review would work in safety-net settings or catch errors in agent interactions conducted in languages other than English.
